svg.text: Sheet 2 of 3 — Low-voltage and signal wiring (3.3 V / 5 V)

Controller, temperature sensor, SSR drive, USB power and the Wi-Fi safety link. Tags D1…D7 match the table. Grove cable colours shown are the usual ones: confirm each wire against the pin with a meter.
Slot in the pocket wall (the only crossing)
left side wall (seen from the front)
2.8" display on the other side (320 x 240, touch)
Find J7 / J10 / J6 by the names printed on the board (GPIO_D, UART1, IIC).
Their order along the edge may differ from this drawing.
SSR control end (3 / 4) faces the display pocket
passes through the round hole in the left side wall
Probe tip in the middle of the
oven, next to the board, in air.
USB-A to USB-C cable, 5 V. Runs OUTSIDE the box and enters through the slot in the left side wall.
• Three Grove (HY2.0-4P) to DuPont cables: one each for J7, J6, J10.
• The SSR is switched on its − side: 3V3 goes to terminal 3 (+) and IO32
sinks terminal 4 (−). A 1 kΩ pull-up on the board keeps it OFF at reset.
• Grove wires are thin: fold the stripped end double or crimp a ferrule
before clamping it under an SSR screw.
• Unused ends (J7 pins 1, 4 and J10 pins 2-4): heat-shrink each one.
• Bench test with USB power only, no mains: the SSR LED must stay off
through reset, and light when the firmware calls for heat.
• MAX6675 header order differs between modules: go by its printed labels.
